# Hide & Seize (hideandseize.com)

> Hide & Seize is a free turn-based stealth game of capture the flag, played in the browser against the computer. You lead Blue's eight players (a Scout, two Runners, a Shadow, two Hunters and two Guards) against Red's eight. Steal Red's flag and bring it back to your base; you can't score while Red has your flag, so tackle whoever is carrying it to send it home. First to 3 points wins; after each point everyone goes back to the start, and the side that lost it moves first.

How it plays: each player has Speed, Sight, Stealth and Strength. You start knowing only your own half of the field, and ground stays on the map once one of your players has seen it. Red's players show only while one of yours can see them: a player sees its sight in squares, less the other's cover, which comes from Stealth, long grass and woods, and from sneaking (a little more cover, fewer moves) or hiding (more cover, no moves). Flag carriers lose their own stealth but still get cover from the ground. Tackling a player next to you succeeds by chance (about 50%, more with more Strength and when you weren't seen); the loser misses 2 turns and comes back at its own base, and a flag carried by whoever is out goes straight home. A player who dodges a tackle is winded for the rest of that turn, so a second tackle is more likely to work. Every game shuffles some of the woods and long grass, so the far side has to be explored. Movement costs 1 a square on grass, long grass and bridges, 2 in woods and on hills, 3 at a ford or in water; rocks block the way. Wading through water soaks a player: 1 less Speed, Sight, Stealth and Strength until the end of its next turn. Picking up a flag takes a move. The computer has two levels, Easy and Normal; like you, it sees your players only through its own and knows only the ground its players have seen.

Maps: five built-in fields (Meadow, Riverbend, Pinewood, Highlands, Old Fort), each 25 by 37 squares, and a map editor (https://hideandseize.com/editor.html) for new ones from 11 by 15 to 45 by 61 squares with 1 to 12 players a side. A map is a small JSON file: format "hide-and-seize-map", version 1, name, author, blurb, shuffle (0 to 0.4) and blueHalf, Blue's half as one line of text per row from the middle row back, where . is grass, , long grass, T woods, ^ hill, # rocks, ~ water, = bridge, : ford, F Blue's flag and s r d h g a Scout, Runner, Shadow, Hunter or Guard; Red's half is Blue's turned 180 degrees. Maps made in the editor are kept in the browser, and can be exported, imported, or sent to adam@hideandseize.com to be added for everyone.

Technical: static files only (index.html, style.css, app.js for the page; rules.js for the rules and ai.js for the computer, neither touching the page; view.js and figures.js for the drawing; maps.js and library.js for the map files; editor.html and editor.js for the editor), MIT-licensed code, no framework, no build step, no backend. Made for a computer with a mouse and keyboard; it runs on phones and tablets with small squares. No account, no ads, no cookies: the game in progress and your maps are saved in the browser.

## Links

- [Hide & Seize](https://hideandseize.com/): the game; How to play (the ? button) gives the rules and answers questions
- [Map editor](https://hideandseize.com/editor.html): make, play, export and import maps
